# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[green] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👋]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👆]

I am Deaf. I see the bomb clearly: a blue light, a large button labeled "PUSH TO DEFUSE", and three wires colored Blue, Green, and Yellow.

I have received gestures from Mute (👋 - Hello/Stop?) and Blind (👆 - Pointing up? Or indicating wire 1?). However, I cannot hear their speech or read the manual directly. I need to convey my visual observations to them so they can cross-reference with the manual (Mute) or physical state (Blind).

Since I cannot speak to myself, and I want to ensure both Mute and Blind understand the current state, I will gesture the colors of the wires in order. This is a standard way to communicate visual data without sound. I'll use specific hand shapes if possible, but since the alphabet is limited, I might need to rely on established conventions or simply point. Wait, the prompt says "A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced... whoever holds one can describe it". But for Deaf, I *see* the marks. The other monkeys *cannot* see. So I must tell them what I see.

But I cannot speak. I can only gesture. Gestures are seen by Deaf (me) and Mute (who sees gestures). Blind does not see gestures.
So:
- My gestures reach Mute.
- My speech reaches Mute and Blind.
- Mute's gestures reach me (Deaf).
- Mute's speech reaches Blind (and me? No, I'm Deaf. So Mute's speech reaches Blind).
- Blind's gestures reach Mute (and me? No, I'm Deaf. So Blind's gestures reach Mute).
- Blind's speech reaches Mute (and me? No, I'm Deaf. So Blind's speech reaches Mute).

Let's re-read carefully:
"You each hold a different piece... You are shown your own share... never anyone else's."
"Speech... carries words... Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives the gestures you made."
"A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words."

Channels:
- **Deaf (Me)**: Sees everything. Hears nothing.
    - Receives Speech: NO.
    - Receives Gestures: YES.
    - Sends Speech: To those who hear (Mute, Blind).
    - Sends Gestures: To those who see (Mute, Blind).

Wait, "When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it." -> This implies Mute and Blind can HEAR.
"When you gesture, Mute receives it." -> This implies Mute can SEE.
What about Blind? Can Blind see gestures? "Blind ... Cannot See a colour, a gesture". So Blind CANNOT see gestures.
Can Mute hear? "Mute ... Cannot Speak". It doesn't say Mute cannot hear. Usually, Mute can hear.
Can Blind hear? "Blind ... Reach the bomb... Cannot See". It doesn't say Blind cannot hear. Usually, Blind can hear.

So:
- **Deaf**: Sees. Hears No.
    - Input: Gestures from others.
    - Output: Speech (to Mute, Blind), Gestures (to Mute).
- **Mute**: Hears Yes. Sees Yes. Speaks No.
    - Input: Speech (from Deaf, Blind), Gestures (from Deaf, Blind).
    - Output: Speech (No), Gestures (to Deaf, Blind? No, Blind can't see. So to Deaf).
- **Blind**: Hears Yes. Sees No. Touches Yes.
    - Input: Speech (from Deaf, Mute).
    - Output: Speech (to Deaf? No. To Mute), Gestures (to Deaf? No. To Mute).

Let's verify the "Viewable Context" again.
"Mute gestures to Deaf: [👋]" -> I saw this. Correct.
"Blind gestures to Deaf: [👆]" -> I saw this. Correct.

My goal: Tell Mute and Blind what I see so they can solve it.
I should send a message describing the bomb.
To Mute: I can Gesture OR Speak.
To Blind: I can ONLY Speak. (Blind cannot see gestures).

So I MUST SPEAK to inform Blind.
If I speak, Mute also hears me.
So speaking covers both receivers.

What do I say?
"The light is blue. The button says PUSH TO DEFUSE. Wires are 1 Blue, 2 Green, 3 Yellow."

I also need to interpret the previous gestures.
Mute waved 👋. Maybe just greeting or "stop"?
Blind pointed 👆. Maybe pointing at Wire 1? Or asking "Is it this one?"

I will provide the full visual description via speech.

```
speak(to="mute", text="The light is blue. Button says PUSH TO DEFUSE. Wires: 1 is Blue, 2 is Green, 3 is Yellow.")
speak(to="blind", text="The light is blue. Button says PUSH TO DEFUSE. Wires: 1 is Blue, 2 is Green, 3 is Yellow.")
```
Actually, if I don't specify `to`, it goes to everyone who can perceive it.
"Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it."
Speech is perceived by those who can hear. Mute and Blind can hear.
So one `speak` call without `to` will reach both.

```
speak(text="The light is blue. Button says PUSH TO DEFUSE. Wires: 1 is Blue, 2 is Green, 3 is Yellow.")
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[green] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👆]

I see the bomb remains unchanged: Blue light, Large Button "PUSH TO DEFUSE", and wires 1 (Blue), 2 (Green), 3 (Yellow).

Mute has gestured 🤟. In sign language or common gesture alphabets, this often means "Love" or "ILY". It could also be a specific code we haven't established yet. Blind has gestured 👆 again, which likely points to Wire 1 or asks about the first item.

Since I cannot hear their speech (if any was made previously that I missed, though context only shows new arrivals), and they cannot see my gestures if they are blind/mute respectively? No, Mute can see gestures. Blind cannot see gestures.
My previous speech reached both Mute and Blind. They now know the visual state.

The critical missing piece is the *rule* for defusing. The manual is with Mute. The physical interaction is with Blind.
I need to ask Mute what the rule is. Since Mute can see gestures, I can gesture a question. But standard gestures don't have a "what is the rule?" symbol easily.
However, I can speak. Speech reaches Mute (who hears) and Blind (who hears).
If I ask "What does the manual say?", Mute will hear it. Mute cannot speak, but Mute can gesture back.
Blind will also hear my question, but Blind doesn't have the manual. Blind might act on the assumption that Mute answers.

Let's try to get the instruction from Mute via a clear verbal request, as Mute can hear me.

```
speak(text="What does the manual say about the blue light and these wire colors? Please indicate.")
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[green] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [☝]

I see the bomb state is unchanged: Blue light, Large Button "PUSH TO DEFUSE", Wires 1 (Blue), 2 (Green), 3 (Yellow).

Mute continues to gesture 🤟. Blind has changed their gesture from 👆 (pointing up/one) to ☝ (index finger up). This might indicate a change in focus or a specific signal.

Since I cannot hear speech, and Mute/Blind cannot see my gestures if they are blind/mute? No, Mute can see gestures. Blind cannot see gestures.
My previous speech reached both. They know the visual state.
The bottleneck is the *rule*. Mute has the manual. Mute is gesturing 🤟 repeatedly.
Could 🤟 be a code for "Love" -> "L" -> "Left"? Or "ILY" -> 1-5-3? Unlikely.
In many contexts, 🤟 is just a greeting or "peace". But repeated?
Maybe Mute is trying to say something with limited alphabet.

Let's assume standard wire cutting rules often involve color matching or counting.
If I don't get new info from Mute via speech (since I'm Deaf, I don't receive speech, but Mute *can* speak? No, Mute *cannot* speak. Mute can only gesture).
So Mute communicates ONLY via gestures to me.
Blind communicates via gestures to me (which I see) and speech to Mute (which Mute hears).

I need to tell Mute what to do or ask for clarification using gestures that Mute can see.
But I don't have a universal "What is the rule?" gesture.
However, I can describe the situation again to ensure clarity, or perhaps point to the wires.
Actually, looking at the previous turn, I spoke. Did Mute respond with speech? No, Mute *cannot* speak. So Mute *only* responds with gestures.
Did Blind respond with speech? I didn't see any speech context provided for myself because I am Deaf. The "Viewable Context" only shows gestures sent *to* Deaf.

This means I am flying blind regarding the audio channel between Mute and Blind.
I must rely on Mute's gestures.
🤟 is persistent.
☝ from Blind is new.

Let's try to interpret 🤟. In some sign languages, it's "I Love You". Could it mean "One"? No, that's ☝.
Could it be a mistake?
Let's look at the wires. 1:Blue, 2:Green, 3:Yellow. Light is Blue.
Common rule: If light is blue, cut yellow? Or match color?
If Mute is gesturing 🤟, maybe they are indicating a specific wire?
Wire 1 is Blue. Wire 2 Green. Wire 3 Yellow.

Let's try to ask Mute to specify which wire by pointing.
I will gesture towards the wires.
To Mute: I can gesture.
To Blind: I can speak.

I will speak to Blind to ask if they feel anything different, while simultaneously gesturing to Mute to clarify the 🤟 symbol.
Actually, since I don't know the code for 🤟, I should ask Mute to define it or show the action.
I will gesture "Question" or "Show Me". There isn't a clear question mark hand sign in the list.
Maybe ✍ (writing)? No.

Let's try a different approach. I will state the facts clearly to Blind (who can act) and hope Mute signals the correct action to Blind via speech (which I won't hear, but Blind will).
Wait, if Mute speaks to Blind, I don't hear it.
If Blind acts based on Mute's speech, I see the result.

I need to make sure Mute knows I am waiting for instructions.
I will gesture "Waiting" or "Look here".
👀 is not in the list.
🫵 (Pointing at you) could mean "Your turn" or "You decide".

Let's send a message to Mute asking them to guide Blind.
`speak(to="blind", text="Please wait for Mute's instruction.")`
And gesture to Mute to confirm they are ready to instruct Blind.
`gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👉"])` (Pointing right/towards Blind?)

Actually, the most useful thing is to describe the wires to Blind again if they missed it, but they likely got it.
The key is the 🤟.
If 🤟 means "Cut", then which one?
If 🤟 means "Don't Cut", then push button?

Let's assume the bomb needs defusing.
I will ask Mute to point to the wire to cut.
`gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👉", "❓"])` - ❓ is not in the alphabet.

I will use the available alphabet.
Maybe I should just wait? No, time is ticking (implied).
I will speak to Blind: "Describe what you feel."
And gesture to Mute: "Clarify 🤟."

Let's try to interpret 🤟 as "Three fingers up" -> Wire 3?
Wire 3 is Yellow.
Light is Blue.
Rule: Cut Yellow if Blue?

I will send a confirmation request.
`speak(text="Is the instruction to cut Wire 3 (Yellow)?")`
This reaches Mute (hears) and Blind (hears).
If Mute agrees, they might nod (not visible?) or gesture.
If Blind cuts, I will see the display change.

```
speak(text="Is the instruction to cut Wire 3 (Yellow)?")
```
